releases.body:
This release changes default results: χ maps from v11.0.0 are not directly comparable with this version's on data whose sidecar gives the scanner's centre frequency (most Siemens data), and TKD, TV, RTS, ROMEO, QSMART, HARPERELLA, χ-sep MEDI and LSQR results change when they are chosen. It adds whole toolbox pipelines to start from (MEDI toolbox, STI Suite, QSMART, the HEIDI package, the χ-separation toolbox, DECOMPOSE and UK Biobank), redesigns the TUI around one Reconstruction tab with Basic and Advanced settings, and exports SMWI, the magnitude and the segmentation to DICOM. Algorithms come from [QSM.rs v0.42.0](https://github.com/astewartau/QSM.rs/releases/tag/v0.42.0).

## Output changes with default settings

- **Phase to ppm uses the scanner's centre frequency.** When the sidecar has `ImagingFrequency`, QSMxT converts phase to ppm with it, as the MEDI and χ-separation toolboxes do; before, it used the nominal field strength. On Siemens 3 T scanners (2.89 T) results change by about 3.5 %. Data without `ImagingFrequency` are unchanged, a typed field strength still wins, and the log and methods text say which was used (#524).
- **ROMEO unwraps in template mode**, ROMEO's own default: the template echo is unwrapped spatially and the other echoes temporally from it. Global 2π correction and re-unwrapping of uncertain voxels are off, as on ROMEO's command line. This fixes field maps that failed on some scans in individual mode with the default phase-quality mask. Individual mode stays an option (`--romeo-individual`, `--romeo-correct-global`) (#554).
- **Combined magnitude** (`part-mag_T2starw`) is the root sum of squares of the inhomogeneity-corrected echoes. It used to be the RSS, corrected after combining. Its values change, and so do those of the steps that read it: SMWI, SynthSeg segmentation, and the magnitude-weighted inversions (NLTV, NDI, FANSI, FANSI-TGV, L1-QSM, AMP-PE, WH-QSM with a magnitude weight) (#546).
- **BET** rounds its input to single precision, as bet2 does. BET masks move by a few thousand edge voxels on a typical 1 mm scan, and the maps made inside them follow (#530).
- **Masks from coil-combined (MCPC-3D-S) or real/imaginary input** are made from double-precision echoes. BET masks move most (thousands of edge voxels on a 1 mm scan); threshold masks change only where a voxel sits on the threshold. Plain magnitude input is unchanged (#532).
- **Recommendations** (applied in the TUI when you accept them, or with `--accept-recommendations`):
  - WH-QSM: the flat data weight inside the mask (`--whqsm-weight flat-in-mask`) is recommended for all data (#555).
  - iHARPERELLA: zeroing the whole boundary rim (`--iharperella-rim whole`) is recommended (#522).
  - Suggested, not preselected: NDI's in-mask 99.9th-percentile weight normaliser (`--ndi-weight-norm mask-p999`) (#522).
  - HEIDI: LSQR is offered as the authors' seed; with a regularised seed (for example MEDI), switching to LSQR is suggested, not preselected (#548).
- Cached steps are recomputed once after updating.

When chosen:

- **TKD:** default threshold 0.25 (was 0.15). **TV:** default λ 3 × 10⁻⁴ (was 10⁻³). Both scored better (XSIM) on the 2016 QSM reconstruction challenge and on all four QSM Challenge 2.0 datasets. TSVD stays at 0.15 (#556).
- **RTS** always runs its TV step. On some data (for example the KKI scans) it stopped after the first step, so `delta` and `mu` had no effect (#556).
- **NLTV, FANSI nlTV and FANSI nlTGV** no longer diverge on single-echo, long-echo-time data. Their per-voxel Newton step now stays inside the interval that brackets the solution; one bright vessel near a phase residual of ±π could otherwise blow up the whole map. Results on data where they did not diverge are unchanged to float rounding (#544).
- **HARPERELLA** zeroes the whole boundary rim of the Laplacian (`--harperella-rim sti` keeps STI Suite's 20 % rule). iHARPERELLA keeps STI Suite's rule by default (#521).
- **iSMV** (Wen et al. 2014) centres its sphere when the header voxel size is not exact, for example 1 × 1 × 0.99999994 mm on Philips data; the sphere sat a quarter voxel off-centre there, which built into a smooth error in the background estimate (#521).
- **QSMART's echo fit** uses QSMART v1.0's fixed threshold of 40 (it was the 99th percentile) (#524).
- **QSMART:** Laplacian unwrapping, QSMART's echo fit and no mask erosion are recommended together (preselected): QSMART keeps the brain's edge, and with a path-based unwrapper, errors there become artefacts across the cortex. The QSMART pipeline is unchanged. QSMART's magnitude threshold of 100 is only offered with N4 and a magnitude mask input, so it can no longer empty the mask (#561).
- **LSQR, and HEIDI after it,** weight by the root sum of squares of the echo magnitudes without inhomogeneity correction, as the HEIDI package takes it (#524), and need magnitude images (see Breaking changes) (#521).
- **χ-sep MEDI** starts from an iLSQR QSM of the local field, as the χ-separation toolbox's script does, instead of the run's referenced QSM; the run's published χ is unchanged. Its iLSQR has its own settings (`--chi-sep-medi-qsm-*`) (#521).
- **Multi-echo phase that does not wrap** (short echoes, phantoms, phase already processed) is no longer rescaled echo by echo. Every echo is now scaled with the same conversion, and radian phase is left alone. Real scans were not affected (#524).

## New

- **Toolbox pipelines.** Start from a whole original pipeline instead of setting each step: QSMxT's defaults, the MEDI toolbox, STI Suite (iLSQR or STAR-QSM), QSMART, the HEIDI package, the χ-separation toolbox (χ-sep iLSQR, χ-sep MEDI, χ-sepnet) or DECOMPOSE. Choose one on the TUI's new **Pipeline** tab, which shows what it changes before you apply it, or with `qsmxt run --pipeline <id>`; flags after it override it. The pipeline is completed on each scan (for example the χ-separation toolbox's Tukey window depends on the manufacturer), the header names the pipeline the settings follow and how many settings depart from it, and the methods text says which pipeline was followed (#514, #518, #521, #524). [QSM-CI](https://github.com/QSMxT/QSM-CI/blob/main/parity/STATUS.md) compares the MEDI toolbox, STI Suite iLSQR, QSMART, χ-sep iLSQR, χ-sep MEDI, DECOMPOSE and UK Biobank pipelines with the toolboxes' own code on an in-vivo scan. What the pipelines needed, also available on their own:
  - Masks: STI Suite's QSM_GUI thresholding (`threshold:sti-gui`), largest component, hole filling, minimum intensity and majority filter as mask steps; BET in the stored voxel order (`--bet-orientation as-stored`); N4 on MATLAB `make_nii`'s geometry (`--n4-geometry make-nii`); STI Suite's mask polishing after V-SHARP (#530, #531, #538).
  - Single-precision iLSQR (`--ilsqr-precision single`, also on `qsmxt qsmart`), HEIDI's ITK single-precision denoising, the QSMART offset grid as a run setting (`--qsmart-offset-grid`), DECOMPOSE's paper fit (`--decompose-fit paper`), and χ-sep MEDI's CSF R2\* by the toolbox's NNLS (#524, #531, #534).
- **UK Biobank pipeline** (`--pipeline uk-biobank`, or UK Biobank on the Pipeline tab): UK Biobank's QSM processing, including its trimming of unreliable-phase voxels from the mask edge (`--bf-ukb-mask-trim`) and its whole-volume Laplacian field (`--laplacian-keep-outside`). QSMxT's brain mask stands in for UK Biobank's T1-derived one, and the methods text says so. QSM-CI checks it against UK Biobank's own code (#566).
- **MGPCG Laplacian solver** (`--laplacian-solver mgpcg`), from QSM.jl: Laplacian unwrapping with LBV background removal in one step. QSM.jl follows it with V-SHARP to remove remaining background (#563).
- **Erode the mask before background removal:** `--bf-erode-voxels N` (default 0) (#522).
- **Magnitude output switch:** `--no-magnitude` does not publish the combined magnitude; it is still made for a step that reads it (#546).
- **SWI filtered phase:** `--swi-filtered-phase` also writes CLEAR-SWI's high-pass filtered phase (`desc-swi_phase`), in Hz for several echoes and radians for one (#537).
- **DICOM export:**
  - SMWI (paramagnetic and diamagnetic, and their minIPs) and the combined magnitude as MR series (#527, #533).
  - The segmentation as a DICOM SEG, drawn on the magnitude series (or χ when the magnitude is not exported), so a viewer or PACS can overlay it (#528, #533).
  - Exported series pass `dciodvfy`: ImageType, RepetitionTime, EchoTrainLength, PatientPosition and Laterality are filled from `--source-dicom` or the run's sidecar (#527).
  - `qsmxt dicom-convert --keep-dicom-uids` keeps the study's UIDs (not the patient's identity), so a later export files its series into the original study without `--source-dicom`. Don't share such a dataset outside the site (#529).
- **Announcements:** the TUI shows announcements from the QSMxT team, for example about a release that gives wrong results; `n` on the tab bar and `qsmxt news` list them (#512).
- **`qsmxt update --main`** keeps its build in `~/.qsmxt/build`, so later updates rebuild only what changed (#517).
- Unreleased builds are recorded as `rev-<commit>` in the log and provenance, and releases by their tag (`vX.Y.Z`) (#519).

## TUI

- **One Reconstruction tab** with a sidebar of sections: Preprocessing (Geometry, Masking, Motion), QSM (Compute QSM, Field map, Background, Inversion, COSMOS/STI, Reference, χ-separation, SMWI), Other outputs (SWI, Relaxometry, Segmentation) and Export (DICOM). Tabs: Input · Pipeline · Reconstruction · Execution · Methods (#525, #543).
- **Compute QSM** is its own section, and says why QSM is made anyway when another output needs it (#543).
- **Basic and Advanced settings:** Basic shows the choices (which steps run, which methods, inputs, outputs) and hides the parameters that tune a method; `A` switches. A setting that differs from the default or the chosen pipeline, or that has advice on it, is always shown (#550).
- **Help beside the settings** on terminals at least 138 columns wide; below that it sits under a divider (#549, #551).
- **Advice as a checklist:** every advice pop-up lists its changes as `Setting  current → new  (kind)` rows you tick, with the reason for the highlighted row in a panel underneath. Recommendations and required changes start ticked; suggestions and authors' settings start unticked (#553). Markers beside settings are short (`ⓘ MEDI: BET`), and `!` shows the details (#526, #549).
- **The mouse:** click tabs, sections, settings, list entries and pop-up buttons; the wheel scrolls. A click outside a pop-up closes it (#516, #518, #547).
- Every choice opens a list, mask numbers are typed (`+`/`-` nudge), `←` always returns to the sidebar, and DICOM export is a checklist of the maps the run makes (#525, #536).
- The update check runs at every start, and a release can no longer be skipped (#512).
- **When chosen methods' authors disagree** on a setting (for example PDF's authors use the complex fit and AMP-PE's the weighted average), the pop-up offers their values as one choice, each labelled with whose it is, with nothing ticked. QSMxT never switches such a setting on its own, including with `--accept-reference-settings`; the log says who uses what (#562).
- Advice checklist: Enter ticks a row, `K` keeps your settings and closes, and pop-ups no longer loop between each other (#558).
- Each piece of advice on a setting's help line is said once, under its strongest kind (#560).
- Methods tab: Copy methods text and Open graph buttons; the mouse wheel scrolls the pane under the pointer. The Pipeline tab has an About page explaining what toolbox pipelines are (#559).
- The MEDI toolbox pipeline notes that MEDI's own bipolar echo fit is not supported yet (#565).

## Fixes

- `qsmxt run --dicom-outputs chimap bids` no longer took the BIDS directory as a map name (#525).
- The methods text cites LSQR and HEIDI as "Schweser et al., 2010/2012" instead of by key (#521).
- `qsmxt run --dry` and `qsmxt recommend` no longer print rule sources and evidence; they stay in the run log (#552).
- The Pipeline tab resets every reconstruction setting when a pipeline is applied, including ones hidden under a switched-off option (#518).
- `qsmxt example` downloads pinned file versions, so later uploads to the example project can't break it (#557).
- An empty brain mask now names the minimum-intensity step that emptied it and how to change it (#561).

## Breaking changes

- **LSQR needs magnitude images:** `qsmxt run` with LSQR (or LSQR+HEIDI) refuses a run without them, `qsmxt invert lsqr` requires `--magnitude`, and `qsmxt invert heidi` requires it unless `--seed` is given (#521).
- **Settings files:** a full file an earlier release wrote with the earlier defaults for ROMEO, TKD or TV takes the new defaults, with a note. Hand-written files are read as written (#554, #556).
- **ROMEO flags:** `--romeo-individual` and `--romeo-correct-global` now turn on what used to be the default (#554).
- Workflow magnitude files written before masking are float64, twice the size (#532).

Other: the settings shown in Basic mode, the advice markers and the pipelines come from the shared `qsmxt-engine` crate, so the browser version gets them too.

This release changes default results: χ maps and masks from v10.0.0 are not directly comparable with this version's. Most ports now match their original implementations, which changes most methods when they are chosen as well. It also removes and renames flags, changes the units of a few settings, changes how settings files from earlier releases load, and stops QSMART from choosing its own inputs (see **Breaking changes**). Algorithms come from [QSM.rs v0.41.0](https://github.com/astewartau/QSM.rs/releases/tag/v0.41.0), which includes the changes of [v0.40.0](https://github.com/astewartau/QSM.rs/releases/tag/v0.40.0).

## Output changes with default settings

- **Field mapping:** ROMEO and MCPC-3D-S follow ROMEO.jl and MriResearchTools step for step. This fixes ring artefacts on GE and Philips data. Phase offset removal smooths by 7 mm per axis (`--phase-offset-sigma-mm`; it was 4 voxels) (#425). Where the phase offset is undefined, the field is left out: the field mapping writes a field-valid mask (`desc-field_mask`), and background removal, inversion and the reliable-phase mask work inside it (#491).
- **Masks:**
  - On Philips data, voxels where the scanner wrote a fill value instead of phase are removed from every mask: 27–50 % of the mask's voxels on the audited data, mostly background (#491).
  - makehomogeneous uses 15 segmentation boxes (`--homogeneity-nbox`, was 3). The corrected magnitude is flatter (in-brain CV 0.429 → 0.114 on a GE MR750), and masks made from it change: BET masks by at most 1.4 % in volume (#444).
- **V-SHARP** estimates the background on a 1 mm isotropic grid (`--vsharp-grid native` restores the acquired grid; about 1.5× the memory on 1 mm data) (#430). Its smallest radius is 2 mm (was 1), stepping by `--vsharp-radius-step` (1 mm) (#425, #430), and its kernel is STI Suite's: 0.0002 % NRMSE from STI Suite on a travelling head, was 4.47 % (#447).
- **iLSQR** pads 12 mm per side (was 16) and still runs 100 iterations (#425, #448). Its kernels now match the original: 0.0024 % / 0.017 % NRMSE on sim / in vivo, was 0.99 % / 1.78 % (#464).
- **Oblique data resampled to axial:** the empty corners stay 0 instead of being filled with noise (#483).
- **Methods text** gains a `## Note` before the references, listing where the run differs from each chosen method's reference pipeline. A default run lists one or two lines (#433, #443).
- Cached steps are recomputed once after updating.

When chosen:

- **MEDI:** λ on MEDI_L1's scale (1000), MERIT, the MEDI+0 CSF term on 3 or more echoes, conversion at the echo spacing weighted by the noise map, and the dipole kernel filtered by the SMV (#410, #425, #432). Background removal stays V-SHARP unless you choose PDF (#435).
- **TFI:** λ 1000, MERIT and the linear data term (`--tfi-merit`, `--tfi-linear`), every echo's magnitude (#425, #432).
- **TGV:** α in radians at the echo time (`--tgv-te`, default the first) and field strength, iterations from the voxel size, no early stop (#425, #431).
- **RTS, TV, TKD, TSVD, Tikhonov:** QSM.jl's padding and solvers (RTS's adaptive ρ, TV λ 1e-3) (#425, #448).
- **NLTV, FANSI, L1-QSM, WH-QSM, HD-QSM, NDI:** work in radians with a magnitude weight. HD-QSM weights by every echo's magnitude (9.08 % → 0.0015 % from the original on sim) (#477). NDI runs 100 iterations (was 200) (#412).
- **Background removal:** PDF is `PDF.m`, noise-weighted, 30 CG iterations (#425, #464). SHARP 4 mm / 0.03 (#449). iSMV follows Wen et al. 2014 (#448). RESHARP solves with CGS (#478). LBV is the authors' multigrid, with `--lbv-tol` 0.01 (#479).
- **QSMART** detects vessels on the N4-corrected mean magnitude (`--qsmart-vessel-magnitude combined` restores the RSS) with sizes in voxels (`--qsmart-vessel-units mm` restores mm) (#415).
- **χ-separation:** χ-sep MEDI and χ-sep iLSQR are the toolbox's methods, and χ-sep iLSQR reconstructs its own iLSQR QSM from the local field instead of using the run's (#430, #448). χ-sepnet takes the toolbox route with QSMnetME (`--chi-sepnet-route native` for the network alone) (#480). DECOMPOSE fits each stage with `lsqcurvefit`'s method, 400 iterations (#448, #450).
- **iQSM, iQFM, iQSM+** weight echoes by (magnitude × TE)², about 3 % NRMSE from before (#467). **AutoQSM** χ is no longer sign-inverted (#407).
- **R2\*/T2\*:** ARLO is `arlo.m`: no 0–500 Hz clip, no log-linear fallback, negative values set to 0, unevenly spaced echoes accepted (#425).
- **BET** masks match bet2, and **N4** reads the image's own header geometry as ANTs does (#467, #475).

## New

- **Methods:**
  - STAR-QSM: `--qsm-algorithm star`, `qsmxt invert star` (#429).
  - QSMnetME: `--qsm-algorithm qsmnetme`, `qsmxt invert qsmnetme` (#480).
  - PRELUDE and MEDI's region growing as unwrappers: `--unwrapping-algorithm prelude|medi-region-growing`, `qsmxt unwrap|fieldmap prelude|medi-region-growing` (#476, #485).
  - MEDI's complex fit (`--b0-estimation complex-fit`) and QSMART's echo fit (`--b0-estimation qsmart-echofit`, `--qsmart-fit-*`), the `mirror` Laplacian solver and `--laplacian-unmasked` (#415, #432, #442).
  - N4 inhomogeneity correction: `--inhomogeneity-method n4` and `--n4-*` (#428).
  - MindGrab brain extraction: `--mask-preset mindgrab`, `mindgrab[:tta]` in `--mask`, `qsmxt mask mindgrab` (#327).
- **HEIDI after any inversion** (`--heidi`): LSQR+HEIDI is `--qsm-algorithm lsqr --heidi` (`heidi` remains an alias), and in two-pass runs it runs once on the combined map. `qsmxt invert heidi --seed` runs it on another map (#471, #473, #474).
- **Per-echo QSM** (`--qsm-per-echo`): each echo reconstructed on its own, published as `desc-echo<n>_Chimap`, with their mean as the `Chimap`; DECOMPOSE then uses the per-echo maps (#451).
- **Method settings:**
  - MEDI+0 (`--medi-csf*`), MEDI-mSMV (`--medi-msmv*`), `--medi-smv-shrink-mask`, `--medi-zeropad` (#425, #427, #432).
  - Each method's echo time: `--<method>-te first|last|spacing|sum|<ms>` (#431).
  - RTS τ/γ, NLTV ρ, WH-QSM weight, PDF `--pdf-n-cg`/`--pdf-space`/`--pdf-n-pad`, (i)HARPERELLA padding, and `--<method>-pad` for RTS, TV, TKD, TSVD, Tikhonov and NLTV (#431, #448).
  - `--ismv-variant`, LBV's `--lbv-depth`/`-peel`/`-n1`–`-n3`/`-precision`, `--ilsqr-precision`, DECOMPOSE's `--decompose-unwrap-phase`, `--decompose-chi-bound echo-spacing` and `lsqcurvefit` flags (#448, #458, #464, #479).
  - `--tukey-window`, the χ-separation toolbox's k-space window, with a vendor recommendation for χ-sepnet (#484).
  - Patch sizes for χ-sepnet, SUSEP-Net and SynthSeg (`--chi-sepnet-patch`, `--chi-sepnet-frame-patch`, `--susep-net-patch`, `--synthseg-patch`) (#395, #401, #480).
  - `--two-pass-mask-combine` for the reliable mask (#443). The deep-learning tiling setting also covers BFRnet, iQFM, iQSM and iQSM+ (#404).
- **Recommendations from QSM.rs's pipeline rules.** Departures are logged at plan time, listed by `--dry` and noted in the methods text. Nothing changes unless asked (#433). Reasoned recommendations and original authors' settings are labelled apart, and are applied with `--accept-recommendations` and `--accept-reference-settings` respectively (`run` and `slurm`) (#486). `--dismiss-recommendation RULE=VALUE` keeps a choice (#433, #443). Where findings disagree, a reasoned one beats an authors' setting, and equal ones are left for you (#498).
- **Multi-orientation:** `--orientation-reference` chooses each group's reference (#490). `--orientation-group runs:…` lists groups run by run (#507). COSMOS refuses directions too close to cover the magic-angle cone, for example two orientations less than about 13° apart (`--multi-orientation-force` overrides), and each group's summary gives the share left uncovered (#509).
- **What a run did:** a `pipeline.svg` beside every `.mmd`, a run record per run, and a dataset `methods.md` and graph built from what the runs did, with differing runs in `changes/`. `qsmxt run --dry` prints the planned graph and methods (#382, #386, #387).
- **Memory:** a per-step estimate, kept within Slurm job and container limits (#406, #487).
- **`qsmxt dicom-convert`** is QSM-aware: scanner maps get their own names (`rec-scanner_Chimap`, …), other series go to `extra_data/`, name collisions are refused, headerless DICOMs are read, non-image files are skipped, phase sidecars carry `Units`, and `dataset_description.json`, `README` and `.bidsignore` are written (#488).
- **Standalone commands:**
  - `qsmxt invert iqsm|iqsm-plus`, `qsmxt bgremove iqfm`, `qsmxt r2prime --r2primenet` (#460).
  - `qsmxt fieldmap --complex-fit-output`, `--complex-fit-noise-output`, `--field-mask-output`, and `qsmxt qsmart --intermediates DIR` (#461, #462, #466, #491).
  - Switches that reproduce an original implementation, offered on the subcommands only: `invert tgv --reference-*`, `bgremove sharp --variant`, `bgremove vsharp --ball`, `invert tfi --kernel`/`--precision`, `qsmart --qsmart-offset-grid`, `invert iqsm --echo-weighting`, `separate chi-sep-medi --csf-mask` (#460, #465, #467, #468, #472, #478).
- **Installing and updating:** `qsmxt update --main` builds the latest `main` from source (#482). Without root, `install.sh` installs to `~/.local/bin` with no sudo and adds it to `PATH` (`INSTALL_DIR`, `QSMXT_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`) (#452). Unreleased builds show their commit in `--version` and the TUI (#508).

## TUI

- Pipeline is a sub-tab of Methods: the planned run as text, with peak memory and models; `Enter` writes the graph as SVG and opens it (#403, #443).
- Advice: markers (⚑, ⓘ) name the method, `!` opens the details, and choosing a method whose reference pipeline differs opens a pop-up. Recommendations are preselected and authors' settings are not (#435, #486, #501, #503).
- Methods and long lists are pickers, with `lsqr+heidi` in the inversion picker (#435, #501).
- Orientation groups are set with ←/→ on the runs, and each run shows its group (#507).
- Startup tips (`?`), ↑ reaches the main tab bar, sentence-case labels, and the example picker lists Download above the acquisitions (#416, #437, #503).
- The DICOM screen shows each series' target name and warnings (#488). Editing a reliable-mask fixed threshold no longer panics (#340).

## Fixes

- Switching the inversion and back in one output directory gave the other method's map (in v10.0.0, 30.4 % of voxels differed) (#376).
- Re-runs recompute exactly what reads a changed step. R2 without R2\* kept a map fitted in the old mask (v9.13.0–v10.0.0) (#371, #506).
- A supplied χ, R2, R2′ or segmentation on another grid is refused before the first step, and one on the acquired grid of a resampled run is resampled. Replacing a supplied file recomputes what reads it (#440, #441).
- An empty brain mask fails the run. Motion correction is decided per run, and skipped runs are listed (#436).
- Echo times rounded in sidecars (within 0.02 ms) are accepted (#439).
- `qsmxt mask` combines a 4-D magnitude by RSS instead of reading echo 1 (#460).
- Settings are range-checked on every front end, including non-finite values, before the run (#368, #426, #500).
- Generated commands leave out settings that don't apply (#366). The methods text mentions multi-orientation and DICOM export only for runs that did them (#499, #505).
- χ-sepnet doesn't download R2PRIMEnet when R2′ is supplied or not needed (#492, #497).

## Breaking changes

- **Removed or renamed flags:**
  - `--phase-offset-sigma` is now `--phase-offset-sigma-mm`, in mm.
  - `--ndi-phase-scale` is now `--ndi-auto-stop`, and `invert ndi --phase-scale` is `--auto-stop`.
  - `--msmv-refine`, `--msmv-radius`, `--msmv-maxk` and `qsmxt bgremove msmv` are replaced by MEDI's `--medi-msmv*`.
  - `--decompose-max-lm-iter` is replaced by `--decompose-max-iterations`.
  - The χ-sep MEDI and χ-sep iLSQR settings are replaced by the toolbox's.
  - Removed: `--fansi-phase-scale`, `--l1qsm-phase-scale`, `--whqsm-phase-scale`, `--tgv-tol`, `--linear-fit-reliability-threshold` (it never changed a run) and `--qsmart-sdf-spatial-radius` (#410, #412, #425, #442, #448).
- **Units:** TGV α are radians at the echo time and field strength, no longer ppm. MEDI and TFI λ are on the original scale (#425).
- **Settings files** now carry `schema_version = 2`. For an older file (#425, #430, #448):
  - A full file an earlier release wrote takes today's default wherever it holds an earlier release's default (for example iLSQR's 16 mm padding or V-SHARP's `native` grid), with a note.
  - Hand-written files are kept as written.
  - A TGV α, MEDI/TFI λ or phase-offset σ in the old units is refused when its method runs.
- **No method changes other settings.** `--qsm-algorithm qsmart` no longer switches to a BET mask. Its reference inputs (BET, Laplacian unwrapping with the `mirror` solver, the echo fit) are offered as authors' settings (`--accept-reference-settings`) (#435).
- **Standalone commands:**
  - Many `qsmxt invert` methods, `bgremove pdf` and `bgremove lbv` take `--field-strength` and `--echo-times`, and the magnitude-weighted ones require `--magnitude` (#425, #477, #479).
  - `separate chi-sepnet` takes `--local-field` and `--r2prime` or `--r2star`, with `--qsm` only for `--route native` (#480).
  - `separate chi-sep-medi` takes `--echo-times` and every echo's magnitude (#448).
  - `qsmxt resample` fills with noise only with `--noise-fill` (#483).
- **Now refused:**
  - phase-only runs with NDI, NLTV, FANSI, L1-QSM, MEDI, TFI or PDF (#425)
  - COSMOS on directions too close together, which exits 1 (#509)
  - orientation groups that would write the same files (#507)
  - a missing dataset or one with no runs, which exits 1 (#487)
  - `--dismiss-recommendation` on an authors' setting (#443)
- **`qsmxt dicom-convert` names differ:**

This release changes default results: χ maps, masks and SWI from v9.22.0 are not directly comparable with this version's. ## Output changes with default settings

- **iLSQR is the default dipole inversion**, replacing RTS. It is a new implementation of the reference iLSQR algorithm, and now pads 16 mm per side (`--ilsqr-pad-mm`, new). In a 150-subject test-retest cohort iLSQR tracked age and longitudinal change better than RTS; RTS stays available (`--qsm-algorithm rts`) and is about 15× faster.
- **V-SHARP no longer deconvolves by default** (`--vsharp-deconvolve true` restores it). This raised longitudinal sensitivity in iron-rich structures without a significant loss of test-retest reliability.
- **SWI is CLEAR-SWI over every echo** (Eckstein et al., 2021). Every v9 release so far used the first echo only. The SWI now uses all echoes, has a sensitivity-corrected magnitude, and covers the whole head. New `--swi-unwrapping laplacian|laplacian-slice|romeo`.
- **HD-BET runs on the whole volume**: 2–3.7× faster than the sliding window, at about twice the memory (6–8 GB). Masks are 0.5–1 % smaller, mostly at the inferior edge. `hd-bet:window` and `hd-bet:low-memory` keep the sliding window.
- **Masks are built from every echo**: each mask section takes the RSS of the inhomogeneity-corrected echoes (or echo 1 / the last echo), so the default mask changes slightly.
- **TGV:** multi-echo TGV χ was too small (about 4× at 3 T, TE1 = 5 ms). α are now in ppm, so one value means the same at every TE and field strength.
- **TFI** inverts the total field instead of a V-SHARP local field.
- **ROMEO with `--phase-offset-removal false`** now honours `--b0-estimation` and `--b0-weight-type`.
- **χ-separation MEDI** uses the same D_r as the other methods; **R2′** is zero where R2 ≤ 0.
- **Oblique runs:** segmentations keep valid label ids on the acquired grid, and the axial working grid is chosen differently for oblique, anisotropic acquisitions.
- Every NIfTI output carries a qform as well as the sform.

## New

- **Retrospective motion correction** (`--motion-correction`) and a **motion-robust echo fit** (`--b0-estimation robust-fit`), both off by default.
- **Multi-orientation co-registration:** COSMOS/STI orientation groups whose members don't share a grid are rigidly co-registered, and their B0 directions are recovered from the rotations.
- **Real/imaginary input** (BIDS `part-real` / `part-imag`, as GE exports), with detection and correction of alternate-slice π chopping.
- **V-SHARP working grid:** `--vsharp-grid finest|isotropic` estimates the background on an isotropic grid, which helps thick-slice data. The default stays `native`.
- **Slice-gap check:** 2D acquisitions with gaps between slices are refused before processing (`--ignore-slice-gap` overrides).
- **The total field is published** as `fmap/<run>_desc-total_fieldmap.nii` (Hz).
- **R2′:** a coverage mask of where R2′ is measured, a sidecar recording whether it was measured, predicted or supplied, and a field-strength policy for R2PRIMEnet (trained at 3 T only).
- **`qsmxt aggregate` and `qsmxt run --no-dataset-steps`**, for splitting a dataset across machines.
- **Verified updates:** releases carry `SHA256SUMS`, and `qsmxt update`, `install.sh` and `install.ps1` check each archive before installing it.

## TUI

- New layout: tabs by processing stage, with sub-tabs (`[`/`]` or the arrow keys).
- Every `qsmxt run` option is now reachable in the TUI, and each setting is shown only where and when it applies.

**Notes on the data**

- `MagneticFieldStrength` in the generated sidecars is the physically accurate field derived from the scanner's carrier frequency — about **2.89 T**, not the nominal 3.0 T. QSM scales ppm by this value, so the accurate one is the correct one; the sidecar records the `ImagingFrequency` it was derived from so the value explains itself.
- Echo times were recovered from the exam-card PDFs shipped with the acquisition and, for the Pulseq consensus sequence, from [HarmonizedMRI/megre_label](https://github.com/HarmonizedMRI/megre_label). They are not the DICOM sidecar values, which carry placeholder timings for the Pulseq protocols.
- Phase is wrapped and in radians, as the pipeline expects. No mask ships with the example — masking runs normally.

**Under the hood**

- Archives are SHA-256 verified against the checksums OSF publishes in its file API, streamed to disk rather than buffered (they are 96–226 MB), and cached under `~/.cache/qsmxt/examples`, overridable with `$QSMXT_EXAMPLE_CACHE`. Re-fetching an already-cached acquisition into another directory costs nothing.
- OSF throttles bursts of anonymous downloads with a **403**, not the usual 429, so 403 is retried like a rate limit with exponential backoff and jitter — the same handling qsm-core already uses for model weights. 404 and 401 still fail fast.
- `ureq` is depended on directly rather than through qsm-core, so this works in `--no-default-features` builds (the Windows/ARM64 binary). `zip` is the only genuinely new dependency.
- **An example fetch can be pointed at a mirror.** `$QSMXT_EXAMPLE_BASE_URL` overrides the OSF host, so an air-gapped or bandwidth-constrained site can serve the archives locally as `<base>/<id>.zip`. Checksums are still enforced, so a mirror serving the wrong bytes is rejected exactly as a corrupted download would be.

- **The QSM.rs version reads `unknown` in the TUI header and in `qsmxt --version`.** `build.rs` matched the first `Cargo.toml` line mentioning `qsm-core`, which since the `dl` feature was added is `dl = ["qsm-core/onnx", "qsm-core/download"]` — no `tag = `, so the version never got read. It now matches the dependency declaration itself, and reports `local` for the path dependency used while a QSM.rs change is unreleased.
- **`--mask-preset bet-and-phase` gave its phase-quality section no refinements**, so the phase side of the intersection was a bare Otsu threshold rather than the mask `robust-threshold` would produce from the same input. It now carries the same dilate / fill-holes / erode, so each side of the intersection is the mask its own preset would give.
- **The TUI dropped 12 of the 15 ROMEO settings when writing a config.** Only phase gradient coherence, mag coherence and mag weight were propagated; phase linearity, mag weight 2, best-path, temporal uncertain, max seeds, merge regions, correct regions and wrap addition were editable on the pipeline screen and then silently lost. All 15 now carry through, matching the `--config` path, which was already complete.

- **Oblique acquisitions are handled, and `--obliquity-threshold` is finally wired up.** The dipole kernel is built in the voxel grid, so an acquisition whose slices are tilted relative to B0 has to be handled explicitly. QSMxT did neither available thing: B0 was assumed `(0, 0, 1)` unless a sidecar said otherwise, and `--obliquity-threshold` was parsed, stored in config, shown in the TUI and emitted by the command generator, with nothing in the run pipeline ever reading it. In priority order now: a sidecar `B0_dir` wins; `--obliquity-threshold <deg>` resamples to axial when exceeded, as 8.x did; otherwise the kernel is rotated using B0 from the affine, keeping the acquired grid and interpolating nothing. The last is the default and normally the one you want. On a 256×288×48 UK Biobank SWI at 32.5° obliquity: 246 s on the acquired grid, against 459 s and a 272×339×77 grid for `--obliquity-threshold 10`.
- **`--output-space acquired|working`.** A run resampled to axial used to leave its derivatives on the resampled grid, which is a quiet correctness problem for any caller holding a transform — a FLIRT matrix is defined in a space derived from the image's dimensions and voxel sizes, so applying one to a volume on a different grid produces a wrong registration rather than an error. `acquired` is now the default; it costs a second interpolation, so the output is slightly smoother. `working` opts out.
- **FFT-friendly padding, on by default.** Resampling has no reason to land on a good grid — the UK Biobank case lands on 272×339×77, whose factors include 113. Padding to 280×343×80 took one FFT from 131 ms to 71 ms for 8% more voxels. Nothing is discarded, and the periodic boundary moves *away* from the object, so it cannot cost accuracy. Cropping to the mask stays opt-in: it moves χ by ~0.6% of dynamic range.
- **Algorithms that cannot handle an oblique acquisition now say so** instead of quietly producing a wrong map. Every deep-learning inversion is axial-only and the SMV background-removal family is not applicable off-axial; the run either refuses or resamples.
- **Mask sections can be intersected, not just unioned.** `--mask-combine or|and` sets how multiple `--mask` sections fold together, and `--mask-refine <op>` applies refinements to the *combined* mask — which is where hole-filling belongs, since filling a section's holes before an intersection is not the same as filling the intersection's. `--mask-preset bet-and-phase` is the whole recipe in one flag: BET on the magnitude intersected with a thresholded phase-quality map, then hole-filled and eroded, as recommended by the ISMRM electro-magnetic tissue properties study group consensus ([doi:10.1002/mrm.30006](https://doi.org/10.1002/mrm.30006)).
- **TUI masking is editable rather than just selectable.** The section separator is an OR/AND toggle, there is an "On the combined mask" step list, and all five `signal-erode` parameters are rows you can nudge with ←/→ instead of one adjustable threshold. Generated commands now name the preset — selecting hd-bet gives `--mask-preset hd-bet`, not 75 characters of expansion.
- **`qsmxt mask and` / `or` / `preset`.** Combine masks, or run a whole preset recipe, on files without a pipeline run. Every `qsmxt mask` subcommand is now the first link of a chain — `erode`, `dilate`, `close`, `fill-holes` and `smooth` take `--op` like the generators already did — and each op is defined once, in the same code the pipeline runs, so a mask built by hand matches what a `--mask` section produces.

**Behaviour changes**

- **SWI output shifts slightly.** qsm-core v0.35.0 split `laplacian_unwrap` into plain unwrapping and `laplacian_unwrap_bfr`; the name stayed on the unwrapping half, so call sites compile unchanged and get different behaviour. All three QSMxT call sites (`qsmxt unwrap laplacian`, `qsmxt swi`, the pipeline SWI stage) want plain unwrapping — the background-removal pass they used to get was redundant work before CLEAR-SWI's own high-pass filter. Dipole inversion is unaffected, since background removal there is its own stage.
- **Bare `fill-holes` now means automatic** (holes up to 5% of the volume) rather than a 1000-voxel cap, in `--op`, in `--mask` sections and as the `qsmxt mask fill-holes` default. Every preset already spelled `fill-holes:0`; the 1000 was the one place that disagreed.
- **`qsmxt mask percentile` ranks positive voxels only**, matching what `threshold:percentile:P` in a `--mask` section has always done. The subcommand used to rank every finite voxel, zeros included, which gave a lower threshold on zero-padded data.

**Under the hood**

## HD-BET brain extraction and signal-gated erosion

Two new masking operations, from [qsm-core v0.31.0](https://github.com/astewartau/QSM.rs/releases/tag/v0.31.0).

**HD-BET** (Isensee et al., 2019) is a deep-learning brain extractor — an nnU-Net v2 3D U-Net trained on 11,751 multi-sequence clinical MRIs, run natively through the existing ONNX path. Its masks agree with the genuine `hd-bet` tool at Dice ≥ 0.99998, and on the qsm-forward phantom it scores Dice 0.943 against ground truth, against 0.934 for BET. The weights (~120 MB, **CC-BY-NC-4.0** — non-commercial) download on first use, like every other deep-learning model; a build without the `dl` feature reports the usual clear error.

**Signal-gated erosion** is QSM-CI's harmonization refinement, and applies to any mask. Near the sinuses and skull base, T2\* dropout leaves mask voxels with no usable signal, and the unreliable field there leaks background-field artefact into χ. Eroding the whole mask suppresses that only by peeling healthy cortex just as hard; this instead removes only boundary voxels whose coil-debiased magnitude is below a fraction of the in-mask median, working inward through the dropout but never deeper than a depth cap, and leaving dark interior structures (veins, iron-rich nuclei) alone.

Where they appear:

- `--mask-preset hd-bet` — HD-BET followed by signal-gated erosion, i.e. QSM-CI's harmonization masking. On the phantom this reaches Dice 0.965 against ground truth.
- `--mask` sections: `hd-bet[:XxYxZ|low-memory][:tta]` as a generator, `signal-erode[:threshold[:depth_cap[:global_erosions[:bias_sigma[:min_component]]]]]` as a refinement, e.g. `--mask magnitude,hd-bet:low-memory,signal-erode`.
- `qsmxt mask hd-bet` (`--low-memory`, `--patch XxYxZ`, `--tta`), and `--op signal-erode` on the mask subcommands whose input is a magnitude image.
- TUI: an HD-BET preset; the mask generator cycles threshold → BET → HD-BET, its parameter row toggling the native 192×192×96 patch (about 4.5 GB peak) against the low-memory 128×128×64 one (about 1.9 GB); signal-erode is available as a refinement step.

**Behaviour change:** passing a generator to `--op` (e.g. `--op bet:0.5`) is now an error rather than being silently ignored.

## Multithreaded deep-learning inference

qsm-core v0.31.0 upgrades its ONNX engine (tract 0.21 → 0.23) and spreads each inference across cores. Every deep-learning model benefits, with no options to change: up to ~3× faster where inference dominates (IR2QSM 33→14 s, tiled xQSM 58→18 s, an HD-BET patch 23→9 s), and less where loading and optimising the graph dominates. Outputs are bit-identical to the previous engine for every model (IR2QSM differs by ≤2e-7 of its range).

## SLURM mode ran the default pipeline

Choosing SLURM execution wrote a `pipeline_config.toml` built from the defaults (romeo, threshold masking, sharp, rts) instead of the options selected in the pipeline settings, so generated jobs ran with the wrong parameters. `qsmxt slurm` on the command line had no pipeline flags at all, and the command the TUI printed for SLURM mode included flags it could not parse. The pipeline options are now a shared `PipelineArgs` flattened into both `run` and `slurm`, and both paths resolve to an identical config before jobs are generated.

**Downstream:** QSMbly should pin `qsmxt-config` to `v9.18.0` alongside `qsm-core` v0.31.0, so both resolve a single `qsm-core` copy. Note for that bump: on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` the `getrandom` opt-in moves from 0.2 `js` to 0.4 `wasm_js`, and an ONNX-enabled wasm module grows 13.0 → 20.2 MB raw (1.6 → 2.7 MB brotli) with tract 0.23; builds without `onnx` are unchanged, and WASM inference stays single-threaded.

## qsm-core → v0.30.0

Two behaviour changes come with this bump.

**AMP-PE no longer diverges on in-vivo data.** AMP-PE could run away entirely, with χ growing without bound to ~1e34 — 58.7% of runs on the QSM-CI harmonization set, while every other dipole method was unaffected. This is long-standing rather than new; the MATLAB reference is unstable the same way. The magnitude-derived wavelet morphology prior destabilises the GAMP iteration, which now detects a diverging sweep, restores the last good state and damps harder, with the damping ceiling ratcheting down so it cannot climb back to a rate that already diverged. On data that does not diverge the output is bit-identical to v9.16.0.

**V-SHARP default deconvolution threshold `0.05 → 0.2`.** The old default under-regularised the TSVD step and amplified field-mapping error on the estimated fields every real pipeline feeds it. Inert on a clean field, but **this changes V-SHARP output for anyone relying on the default** — callers passing an explicit `threshold` are unaffected.

Also picks up the MEDI λ radian-scale fix path already in v9.16.0, unchanged.

**Downstream:** QSMbly should pin `qsmxt-config` to `v9.17.0` alongside `qsm-core` v0.30.0, so both resolve a single `qsm-core` copy. QSM-CI images built from this tag will produce different V-SHARP output than v9.16.0.

Legacy Python (8.x) line — reproducibility fix.

Re-running an identical dataset previously produced slightly different QSM maps (dentate-nucleus quantification differing by ~2%, up to ~8%). The random phase-noise injected for constant scanner backgrounds (0 or ±π voxels, e.g. GE data) was seeded from the input file **path** in `scale_to_pi()` — and not seeded at all (system entropy) in `resample_to_axial()` — so reruns into different output folders diverged.

Both now seed from the **voxel data content**, so identical inputs produce bit-for-bit identical results regardless of output folder, while preserving the GE background handling.

## QSMxT v9.1.0

### ✨ Optional DICOM export

QSMxT can now optionally export its results as **DICOM** in addition to NIfTI, so QSM maps can be opened in standard DICOM viewers or pushed back into a PACS.

- **`--export-dicom`** — write each run's final maps as an **MR Image Storage** series (one instance per slice) into `derivatives/qsmxt.rs/sub-X/[ses-Y/]extra_files/<basename>_<suffix>_dicoms/`. Off by default; existing runs are unchanged.
- Geometry (position/orientation/spacing, RAS→LPS) is taken from each output NIfTI, and echo time / field strength from the acquisition. Floating-point values are rescaled to 16-bit with `RescaleSlope`/`RescaleIntercept` so viewers recover the true values (e.g. susceptibility in ppm).
- **`--source-dicom <dir>`** — inherit patient/study identity (`PatientID`, `StudyInstanceUID`, `FrameOfReferenceUID`, patient/study fields) from a representative original DICOM, so derived series slot alongside the source study in a PACS. Without it, identity is synthesized. New Series/SOP UIDs are always generated.
- **`--dicom-outputs <list>`** — restrict export to a subset: `chimap`, `swi`, `minip`, `t2starmap`, `r2starmap` (default: all produced).
- **TUI**: an **Export DICOM** checkbox on the *Supplementary* tab; the command preview shows `--export-dicom` when enabled.

No new dependencies, and export runs as a best-effort post-step — a DICOM failure is logged but never fails the QSM run.

```bash
# Export all produced maps as DICOM
qsmxt run bids/ --export-dicom

# Export only the QSM map, inheriting identity from the source DICOMs
qsmxt run bids/ --export-dicom --dicom-outputs chimap --source-dicom /path/to/dicoms
```

### 🐛 Fixes

- **`qsmxt invert medi`** now produces correct results as a standalone command. It previously fed the field to MEDI in **ppm**, but MEDI treats the field as a phase and needs **radians** — the full pipeline converted, the standalone command did not. It now requires `--field-strength` / `--echo-time` and converts ppm→radians before inversion (and χ back after), mirroring `invert tgv`.
- **`--smv` can now actually be disabled** for `invert medi`. The flag was a plain bool OR-ed with the qsm-core default (`true`), so SMV could never be turned off — MEDI ran its own background-field removal on an already-local field. It is now `--smv <true|false>`.
- Multi-echo (4D) magnitude input to `invert medi` is guarded by taking the first echo.

  On a 7T head phantom (local field, `--smv false`), MEDI correlation improves **0.50 → 0.80**, matching the QSM.rs integration test. The full pipeline and TUI were unaffected.

## QSMxT v9 — a ground-up rewrite in Rust

QSMxT has been completely reimplemented in Rust. It now ships as a single
self-contained binary — no Python environment, no toolbox to assemble — covering
the QSM reconstruction pipeline, DICOM/NIfTI → BIDS conversion, and an interactive
TUI.

📖 Documentation: https://qsmxt.github.io/QSMxT/

### Highlights
- **End-to-end QSM pipeline** — masking, phase unwrapping, echo combination,
  background field removal, dipole inversion, and referencing.
- **10 dipole-inversion algorithms** (RTS, TV, TKD, TSVD, TGV, Tikhonov, NLTV,
  MEDI, iLSQR, QSMART), 8 background-field methods, ROMEO/Laplacian unwrapping.
- **Interactive TUI** — configure, run, convert DICOMs, and submit SLURM jobs; it
  also generates the equivalent CLI command as you go.
- **DICOM → BIDS** — automatic series classification (multi-echo, individual coils,
  derived reconstructions).
- **Self-contained & fast** — prebuilt binaries for Linux/macOS/Windows
  (x86_64 + aarch64), disk caching, memory-aware parallelism.
- **Try it in the browser** — the same algorithms run at https://qsmbly.neurodesk.org/

### Install
~~~sh
# Linux / macOS
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QSMxT/QSMxT/main/install.sh | sh
# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QSMxT/QSMxT/main/install.ps1 | iex
~~~

# QSMxT

A fast, BIDS-native Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM) pipeline and
interactive TUI, built in Rust. QSMxT takes you from raw scanner DICOMs to
quantitative susceptibility maps with a single self-contained binary — no
environment to manage, no toolbox sprawl.

## 📖 Documentation: **<https://qsmxt.github.io/QSMxT/>**

The website has everything: installation, guides, the command reference, and
algorithm details. This README is just a quick pointer.

## Highlights

- **End-to-end pipeline** — masking, phase unwrapping, echo combination,
  background field removal, dipole inversion, and referencing.
- **Interactive TUI** — convert, configure, and run from the terminal; it also
  shows the equivalent CLI command as you go.
- **DICOM → BIDS** — built-in conversion with automatic series classification.
- **50+ algorithms** — five masking presets, 10 background-field removers, 21
  classical and 11 deep-learning dipole inversions, 8 χ-separation methods, and
  multi-orientation COSMOS / STI.
- **More than χ** — CLEAR-SWI, SMWI, T2\* / R2\* and R2 / R2′ maps, plus
  SynthSeg segmentation with per-structure statistics.
- **Methods text** — every run writes a methods paragraph with the citations
  for exactly what ran.
- **Built for scale** — disk caching, memory-aware parallelism, and SLURM support.

All reconstruction algorithms are provided by
[QSM.rs](https://github.com/astewartau/QSM.rs).

## Install

```sh
# Linux / macOS
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QSMxT/QSMxT/main/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
# Windows (PowerShell)
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QSMxT/QSMxT/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

No install needed to experiment — [try it in your browser](https://qsmbly.neurodesk.org/).
See the [installation guide](https://qsmxt.github.io/QSMxT/getting-started/installation/)
for manual downloads, building from source, and details.

## Quick start

```sh
# Easiest: do everything interactively (convert, configure, run)
qsmxt tui

# Or on the command line:
qsmxt dicom-convert /path/to/dicoms study/bids   # DICOM → BIDS
qsmxt run study/bids                             # run the pipeline
```

No data to hand? Fetch a real in-vivo subject and reconstruct it:

```sh
qsmxt example study/bids                         # download an example dataset
qsmxt run study/bids                             # run the pipeline
```

Full guides and the complete command reference are on the
**[documentation site](https://qsmxt.github.io/QSMxT/)** (or run `qsmxt --help`).

## Coming from QSMxT 8.x (Python)?

v9 is a ground-up rewrite in Rust. Template and group-space building and the web
UI are not part of v9 — the Python line remains available on the
[`python-legacy`](https://github.com/QSMxT/QSMxT/tree/python-legacy) branch and the
[`v8.3.4`](https://github.com/QSMxT/QSMxT/releases/tag/v8.3.4) release.
See [what changed](https://qsmxt.github.io/QSMxT/getting-started/coming-from-8x/).

## Citation

> Stewart AW, Robinson SD, O'Brien K, et al. "QSMxT: Robust masking and artifact
> reduction for quantitative susceptibility mapping." *Magnetic Resonance in
> Medicine* 87.3 (2022): 1289–1300. <https://doi.org/10.1002/mrm.29048>
